To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the self-image and sexuality of Chinese women with BC changed during the first year after diagnosis; 2) three self-image and sexuality trajectories were identified, with most women showing stable self-image and sexual functioning; and 3) women with low initial self-image showed significantly greater 6-year psychosocial distress.

Women with high self-image and high sexuality scores during acute illness phase have better long-term self-image, sexuality and psychosocial outcomes; women with low self-image and low sexuality scores during acute phase had significantly greater long term psychological distress.

the degree and determinants (TDM difficulties and treatment outcome satisfaction) of change in body self-image and sexuality over the acute illness phase of BC diagnosis and surgery predicted long-term psychosocial outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the diagnosis and treatment of breast cancer on the self-image and sexuality of women with breast cancer.
the psychological impact of BC on women and their family members.
the relationship between the self-concept and the experience of breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self-image is an important predictor of long-term psychosocial outcomes in Chinese women undergoing treatment for early stage BC.
self-image during acute illness predicts long-term outcomes.
the results of this study indicate that self-image and sexuality trajectories during the first year after surgery for breast cancer are associated with 6-years psychological and physical outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

women with breast cancer should be encouraged to be involved in their treatment decision-making process, to be optimistic and to be satisfied with treatment outcomes, in order to have a better body image, and to be less psychologically distressed.

women who are more satisfied with treatment outcomes and who are less troubled by decision making are more likely to experience a more rapid return to their pre-illness self-image, and to experience a more sustained recovery of their sexuality.
self-image and sexuality are important for long-term outcomes, and that interventions should focus on minimizing the decrement in these areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
women with breast cancer should be supported to maintain a positive self-image and high level of sexual function during the acute illness period, as these will predict better long-term outcomes.

self-image and sexuality are stable during the first year after diagnosis of breast cancer, but women with low self-image at diagnosis may have worse long-term psychosocial outcomes, and women with TDM difficulties may experience worse long-term self-image and sexuality.

women who experience a high level of psychological distress and dissatisfaction with treatment outcome during acute illness phase are more likely to experience a high level self-image and sexuality decrement.
